reachability: Assets in the same VLAN reach each other directly.
Assets in different VLANs reach each other only through a device whose role is router or l3-switch with an up layer-3 interface in both VLANs; the lowest-id qualifying router is used.
Routed VLANs are derived offline from each device's interface names.
Firewall and access-control rules are not read, so a route that crosses a router shows only that the two VLANs are routed, not that traffic is permitted.
limits: Firewall and access-control rules are not read.
Attacks that need an account (privileges) or a user action are not modelled.
CVSS v4 Attack Requirements cannot be read (no vector string is stored), so a v4 CVE is judged on its other fields; such CVEs are kept, not discarded.
The NIST IR 7788 mapping is coarse (three values), so many routes tie.
The mapping is applied beyond the CVSS version it was written for.
Only the single highest-likelihood route is kept per target and start.
Spare-port lists are truncated by the checklist, so a start may stand for more ports than it lists.
Assets with no known VLAN are left out of reachability.
An unverified asset is shown as unverified, not as safe.
